steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Demand is the quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price over a period of time.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Law of demand: as price rises, quantity demanded falls (inverse relationship), shown by a downward-sloping demand curve.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Factors shifting demand: income, tastes/fashion, price of substitutes and complements, population, advertising.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Movement ALONG the curve = price change (affects quantity demanded). SHIFT of the curve = non-price factor change (changes demand at every price).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between a movement along the demand curve and a shift of the demand curve. | Describe three factors that could cause an increase in demand for electric cars. | Analyse how a rise in petrol prices would affect demand for public transport and demand for large cars.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Movement along: caused ONLY by price change (e.g. coffee falls from £3 to £2, consumers buy more). steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: ALWAYS distinguish 'demand' (whole curve) from 'quantity demanded' (a point). Price change = movement; other factor = shift. When explaining shifts, specify DIRECTION: right = increase, left = decrease. Substitutes: price of A rises → demand for B rises. Complements: price of A rises → demand for B falls.
